public_rationale: The factual core holds: OpenAI expanded GPT-4 access while interpretability researchers acknowledged substantial unexplained behavior. The [deployment announcement](https://community.openai.com/t/gpt-4-api-general-availability-and-deprecation-of-older-models-in-the-completions-api/289518) and [research update](https://transformer-circuits.pub/2023/july-update/) establish that conjunction. They do not establish that deployment was morally or practically too fast.
limitations: Support applies to deployment proceeding despite incomplete understanding.
The judgment expressed by rushing is not independently scored.
The interpretability update supplies a publication month, not an exact day.

our_interpretation: The testable plain reading is that deployment was expanding despite substantial gaps in understanding model behavior and mechanisms.
Whether that expansion was excessively fast is an evaluative judgment, not a separately measurable fact.
For this ongoing observation, use July–September 2023, the latest completed calendar quarter before publication, as the reporting window. Marcus did not specify this window.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous records show expanding public deployment alongside acknowledged, substantial gaps in understanding how the deployed class of models behaves.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Records show that deployment was not materially expanding, or that the relevant behavior and mechanisms were already comprehensively understood.

Researchers explicitly acknowledged unresolved explanations for language-model behavior while deployment was expanding. The page specifies July only; available_at uses the month's final day as a conservative availability bound.
